cover.thesis:
I turn cultural signals into
commercial fashion stories.
cover.brands: GAP · Banana Republic · Lee Cooper · Poetry · Rare Earth · Old Khaki

ticker: Trend is the signal · Product is the translation · Story is the reason · Customer is the point · Not just what sells — why it sells ·

trend.title:
It starts with
a signal.
trend.text: Streets, stores, screens — culture announces itself long before the spreadsheets do. I read shop floors the way analysts read reports.
chips: “The wall states its thesis: product as identity.”
“One style per lightbox — density is a pricing signal.”
“IP tees priced as fandom. The license is the margin story.”

product.title:
Then it becomes
product.
product.text: The unglamorous middle of fashion is where I live: from trend board to bulk production without losing the idea on the way.
product.brands: Run across GAP · Banana Republic · Lee Cooper · Poetry · Rare Earth · Old Khaki — apparel, accessories, bags.

story.title:
Then it needs
a story.
story.text: A rack without a story is inventory. The lab is where I take a decision further than the brief asked.
story.labText: Metro workwear assumes the day ends at the office. It doesn't. One crease-tolerant blazer that reads sharp at 10am and relaxed at 10pm — plum · bone · ink, good-better-best ladder, camisole within arm's reach.
story.chain: shirt → styling story → attach product → persona → placement → content hook
story.dare: Give me 30 days and an underperforming category: diagnose, decode, rebuild, retell, measure.

customer.title:
It ends with
a person.
customer.text: Everything upstream is judged in one moment — she says yes, or she doesn't. Merchandising is the craft of earning that yes, repeatably.

work.title: The work

featured.code: NK-001 · Indo Spanish Marketing Services · 2024 — present
featured.title:
Launching a brand
that didn't exist

steps.p: Take an entirely new concept — a car fashion brand with no category precedent — from idea to market. No playbook existed; entry had to land.
Product development and trend analysis, sourcing and vendor management, merchandising and buying, and the production workflows connecting them.
A first-of-its-kind range means building the process while running it — every approval, costing and timeline defined from zero.
A successful market entry for a concept the market hadn't seen. [ADD VERIFIED RESULT — range size, doors, sell-through]

featured.nextP: Build the repeat-purchase architecture: attach accessories to the hero range, set a drop cadence, and turn first buyers into a community.

cases.title:
Three brands,
one production engine
cases.intro: For Cape Union Mart's Poetry, Rare Earth and Old Khaki — apparel, accessories and bags across complex, overlapping production cycles.
bullets: Owned development, sourcing and order execution from sampling to bulk
Negotiated vendors for cost-effective, high-quality manufacturing
Coordinated design, logistics and QA into one workflow
Ran trend analysis and market research feeding product planning

cases.title:
The Gap Inc.
discipline
cases.intro: Enterprise merchandising rigor, learned where mistakes cost whole seasons.
bullets: Coordinated sampling for Gap Inc. and Banana Republic with trend compliance
Managed BOMs and approvals across the product lifecycle
Streamlined sample tracking and buyer updates on PLM Centric

work.motto:
The work is done.
The thinking isn't.

about.title:
Designer's eye,
buyer's nerve
about.p1: Naziya trained as a designer before she became a merchandiser — a B.Des in Fashion Design from MJRPU Jaipur (graduated A+), with an ATDC diploma sponsored by Gap Inc. along the way. It shows: she reads garments like a designer and cost sheets like a buyer.
about.p2: Four years in, her range runs from Gap Inc. sampling rooms to launching a brand nobody had a template for. She's happiest on a shop floor, reading what the racks are saying — and the habit doesn't switch off.
about.quote:
“Every product has a customer.
Find the reason they care.”
